Travel & transport

train noun

modern

M-O s.v. train

trāmen, trāminis n.

noun, third declension

Train in modern Latin. Morgan–Owens traces the lexical form trāmen to Charisius; the railway sense is modern. Related vocabulary: trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — draw or pull.

Examples

  • Trāmine īmus.

    We’re going by train.composed

  • Trāmen advenit.

    The train is arriving.composed

Other words

  • trāmen ferriviārium — railway train

    also used · modern

  • hamaxostichus, hamaxostichī m.

    noun, second declension · also used · modern

    A competing learned Neo-Latin term for a train.

See also railway, train station, tram.

SourcesMorgan–Owens: train · Morgan–Owens: Silva

The example sentences marked “composed” are ours.
